tasks.gr11-factors-of-production-t1: Topic: Factors of production and remuneration. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover the four factors (land, labour, capital, entrepreneurship), their characteristics and mobility, and their corresponding remuneration forms (rent, wages/salaries, interest, profit). Include South African examples such as mineral resources, the National Minimum Wage, and SMME entrepreneurship. Ask data-response questions on factor allocation, short-answer identification questions, and policy paragraphs on factor market issues.
tasks.gr11-gdp-gni-t1: Topic: GDP, GNI and Gross Value Added. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover GDP as the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders; the three measurement approaches (expenditure, income, production/output); GNI = GDP plus net factor income from abroad; Gross Value Added (GVA) by sector. Include nominal vs real GDP, GDP per capita calculations, graph interpretation of SA economic output data, and policy paragraphs on using GDP as a measure of economic well-being.
tasks.gr11-mixed-economy-t1: Topic: South Africa's mixed economy and economic structure. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover the three economic systems (market, command, mixed), characteristics of SA's mixed economy, the roles of the private sector and public sector, public goods, merit goods and demerit goods, the structure of SA's economy across primary/secondary/tertiary/quaternary sectors, and government policy choices including the National Development Plan (NDP).
tasks.gr11-infrastructure-exclusion-t1: Topic: Infrastructure and economic exclusion. Grade 11 Economics CAPS. Cover the types of infrastructure (economic: roads, ports, energy; social: schools, hospitals), how infrastructure underpins economic development, the apartheid legacy of spatial economic exclusion, current SA infrastructure challenges (Eskom load-shedding, municipal service delivery, water scarcity), and policy responses to address economic exclusion (RDP, GEAR, ASGISA, NDP).
tasks.gr11-population-labour-force-t1: Topic: Population and labour force (Grade 11 Economics, Term 1). Cover the characteristics of the population (size, growth, age structure, sex, urban and rural), its importance (labour supply, consumers, tax base, dependency), the working-age population (15 to 64), the labour force (employed plus unemployed), the unemployed (no work, available and looking), people not economically active, and the rates: participation rate = labour force ÷ working-age population × 100, unemployment rate = unemployed ÷ labour force × 100, absorption rate = employed ÷ working-age population × 100 and the dependency ratio. Use small imaginary data and give all the numbers in the question. Ask Grade 11 learners to classify people and calculate the rates.
